newsitem.title: UK: Shell shares hit record high pre-results.
newsitem.headline: Shell shares hit record high pre-results.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport and Trading Group Plc jumped more than two percent to a record high on Wednesday, boosted by expectations the oil major may beat analysts' profit estimates after rival British Petroleum pleased investors yesterday.
Shell reports half-year results on Thursday.
By 0841 GMT, Shell gained 11p to 469p on volume of 3.8 million, the second most active FTSE 100 stock behind BP.

"We saw some results from the U.S. majors that were above expectations and BP was well above, so people are thinking Shell could also report above expectations," said Shawn Reynolds, equities research analyst at Lehman Brothers.
Royal Dutch/Shell Group is expected to post net income between 1.265 billion and 1.48 billion pounds for the second quarter, analysts said.
The group reported comparative earnings of 1.187 pounds in the same 1996 quarter.
Other oil integrated stocks rallied and the sector contributed the most points with 12 to the FTSE 100's early rally of about 30 points.
BP shares rose 19p to 880-1/2, extending its rally from yesterday, and Burmah Castrol jumped 13-1/2p to 10.81 stg.

The sector continued to garner support from BP's results on Tuesday when it reported second quarter profits of 740 million pounds, against the most optimistic analysts' forecasts of 690 million pounds.

BP also said it planned to buy back some $500 million worth of shares before the 1998 annual shareholders meeting. The oil company will then seek approval for a broader policy to buy-back shares from "time to time".
"Everybody is going to have to raise BP's estimates for 1997 if not for 1998," Reynolds said.
"The share buy-back is a very strong sign that the management feels it will comfortably meet its own aggressive financial targets and in typical BP fashion, will exceed them," he said.
Reynolds has a "hold" rating on Shell and an "outperform" on BP.
